findings.original_issue: Positivity of gross returns and compact fractions alone did not state the integrability and attainment conditions needed for a finite positive value coefficient. Nonintegrable tails can invalidate that conclusion outside the finite examples.
findings.author_resolution: Restricted the return law to finite support and required continuous positive gross factors on the compact fraction set. Explicitly derived uniform positive/finite bounds, finite continuous expected utility and attained maxima.
findings.peer_verification: Read final paragraph and verified it supplies the needed finite-horizon assumptions. Positive scaling preserves utility order for gamma greater than one. All numerical finite-tree cases and their independent comparisons remain unchanged.

proof_and_instruction_audit: Currency-surplus mean-variance criterion states inverse-CU gamma, covariance sign and unspanned residual; one-dimensional clipping is not generalized to vector clipping.
Positive log-resource domain, exactly spanned nontradable endowment, exposure-versus-cash distinction and opposite financial-fraction lifecycle comparisons are explicit; no universal age rule.
Finite-support homothetic induction now has finite value/attainment conditions; period fractions may repeat while dollar quantities change. Average log variance is not terminal wealth safety.

Bellman upper bound and attaining continuation argument preserves nonanticipation and requires the observed opportunity state. Initial zero-premium exposure hedges state-dependent marginal continuation value; log additive continuation is independent of the initial trade here.
Initial and child return laws straddle safe return, supporting positive state prices; physical probabilities are not confused with pricing probabilities.
Post-fee target formulas have correct buy/sell signs; proportional-cost objective and no-trade interval are conditional one-period models with a real cash-funded ceiling.
Robust lower-mean endpoint uses long-only exposure; narrowed uncertainty kink, alternative high-mean performance and lack of confidence interpretation are explained.

All eight problems are taught before use, complete determinate solutions reconcile, and open memo critique has explicit evaluative criteria; answered retention and extension do not promise a personalized investment policy.
